extracted.intended_audience: researchers and graduate students in foundations and philosophy of mathematics (constructivism vs classical mathematics)
extracted.subtask_description: Scholarly analysis of the debate between intuitionistic/constructive mathematics and classical mathematics, explicating key terms, narratives, and evaluative criteria used by proponents and critics (Bishop, Dummett, Heyting, Pourciau, Richman, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Debasement of meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: The cardinal sin of the classical opposition, from Cantor to Keisler, committed with LEM (law of excluded middle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Term occurs in Bishop’s Schizophrenia and Crisis texts; used by constructivists to charge classical mathematics with producing statements that lack genuine (numerical) meaning when LEM is employed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamentalist excluded thirdist
rubrics_metrics.description: Refers to a classically-trained mathematician who has not yet become sensitized to implicit use of the law of excluded middle (i.e., excluded third) in his arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used pejoratively in constructivist discourse (term appears in Richman’s text, not clearly in Bishop’s); signals failure to recognize non-constructive steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idealistic mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: The output of Platonist mathematical sensibilities, abetted by a metaphysical faith in LEM, and characterized by the presence of merely a 'peculiar pragmatic content'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast with 'realistic mathematics' in Bishop’s lexicon; used to criticize classical results as lacking empirical or computational content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integer (as foundation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The revealed source of all meaning, posited as an alternative foundation displacing both formal logic, axiomatic set theory, and recursive function theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In Bishop’s system integers are emphasized over the continuum; integer-based (numerical) meaning is privileged and said to escape certain criticisms leveled by constructivists (Kronecker allusion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: A Bishopian term (often misunderstood) evoking the opposite of 'schizophrenia'—a healthy constructivist mindset characterized by certain virtues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bishop links integrity to (a) rejection of common sense in favor of formalism, (b) the debasement of meaning, and (c) other ills (excluding dishonesty); root is identical with 'integer'—possible pun indicating primacy of integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law of excluded middle (LEM)
rubrics_metrics.description: The main source of the non-constructivities of classical mathematics; every formalisation of intuitionistic logic excludes LEM, and adding LEM back returns us to classical logic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central pivots of the debate: identifying uses of LEM in a proof or framework diagnoses it as classical/non-constructive; many explanations and examples in surrounding text (see Subsection 3.1 and elsewhere).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited principle of omniscience (LPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: A weak form of LEM involving LEM-like oracular abilities limited to the context of integer sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Still unacceptable to a constructivist, but posited as a potential basis for meaningful dialogue between Brouwer and Hilbert; see discussion in Subsection 3.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning (Bishopian sense)
rubrics_metrics.description: A philosophic term in Bishop’s lexicon that routinely precedes investigation of truth and is conflated with 'numerical meaning' in his writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by Bishop to evaluate mathematical statements; if a statement lacks 'meaning' (in this sense) it may be dismissed regardless of classical coherence—this conflation is central to Bishopian critique of classical mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of a theorem admitting a proof based on intuitionistic logic, expressing computationally meaningful facts about the integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences noted in the text: (1) enables constructivists to blur distinction between pre-LEM and post-LEM numerical meaning and to dismiss certain classical theorems as lacking meaning; (2) allows constructivists to ally with anti-realist philosophies (e.g., Dummett) despite tensions with other realist claims of Bishop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peculiar pragmatic content
rubrics_metrics.description: An expression (from Bishop) connoting an alleged lack of empirical validity of classical mathematics when classical results function merely as 'inference tickets' used in deducing other results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Billinge analyzes this phrase; used to argue classical mathematics may have pragmatic/formal utility without delivering genuine computational or empirical content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic mathematics
rubrics_metrics.description: In Bishop’s lexicon, the realist position (as opposed to idealistic), identified with constructive mathematics based on natural numbers and with claims that constructive theorems describe an external reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bishop sometimes frames constructive mathematics as realist (e.g., natural numbers 'the same in another universe'); used to challenge anti-realist interpretations and to respond to indispensability arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurrection (anti-realist narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: The anti-realist account (following Dummett) that traces the original sin of classical mathematics to LEM and argues that accepting Dummett’s manifestation requirement leads naturally to intuitionistic semantics (truth = verifiability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames intuitionism as a philosophical corrective to a hidden metaphysical assumption in classical practice; used to justify rejection of LEM on philosophical grounds rather than purely mathematical ones.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insurrection (realist narrative)
rubrics_metrics.description: The realist account (aligned with Bishop) that situates intuitionism as a challenge within mathematics that aims to preserve external reality claims while reforming methods (constructive program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portrays constructive mathematics as compatible with describing external reality; used to rebut anti-realist conflations and to argue constructivism can address Quine-Putnam indispensability concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intuitionism as companion to classical mathematics (Heyting’s 'good right')
rubrics_metrics.description: The position that intuitionism should be studied as part of mathematics and has 'a good right' to its conception—i.e., it is one legitimate foundational framework among others, not claiming monopoly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heyting’s dialog (Class and Int) argues classical mathematicians should 'admit the good right' of intuitionistic conception; this stance supports treating intuitionism as a complementary perspective and acknowledges compensations (subtle distinctions, new methods) for 'mutilation' of classical results.
